A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 31-page versions of VLBiMan, including Appendices A–D. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable comparison of the same research work, including equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v3 reports original real-robot experiments on ten bimanual tasks, component ablations, and additional robustness and cross-embodiment results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains the original real-robot success rates, ablations, robustness analyses, and cross-embodiment experiments reported in v3.

M1.justification: The decomposition, vision-language anchored adaptation, and trajectory-composition pipeline in Section 3 is unchanged. Appendix B retains the same orientation-estimation algorithm and closed-loop grasping procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ten tasks, object variations, robotic embodiments, and disturbance conditions. Appendix coverage of lighting changes, varied object geometries, clutter, and partial occlusion is identical.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 5 retain Mechanisms, MAGIC, Robot-ABC, ReKep, and ReKep+ as comparators. The ablation comparators also remain unchanged; the newly cited works are not added to any evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings are identical, including success-rate metrics, 25-trial main comparisons, 20-trial appendix evaluations, interference conditions, and the pre-grasp-only interpolation-density protocol in Table 7.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix C retain the same component ablations, error breakdown, lighting and interference analyses, synchronous-execution comparison, object-anchor and clutter case studies, and interpolation-density ablation.

E5.justification: Trial counts and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version reports seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the success-rate comparisons.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are unchanged, including the appendix results. For example, Table 1 retains 85.3% and 78.0% average success without interference for same-object and novel-instance testing, respectively.

T1.justification: The mathematical formalization, invariant-skill condition, adaptation and trajectory equations, and image-moment calculations in Algorithm 1 are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about one-shot manipulation without retraining, skill composition, robustness, and cross-embodiment transfer.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability boundaries are unchanged, including rigid-object restrictions, execution-recovery and hardware limitations, and Appendix C's discussion of human refinement and robustness mechanisms.

D1.justification: Hardware specifications, demonstration collection, camera settings, orientation estimation, grasp-stabilization details, and interpolation parameters remain identical. Project and supplementary-material access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to Zhou and Jia (2026), 'One-shot real-world demonstration synthesis for scalable bimanual manipulation,' and Zhou et al. (2026), 'Yoto++: Learning long-horizon closed-loop bimanual manipulation from one-shot human video demonstrations.' Their bibliography entries are added on page 16, without substantive new discussion or revised positioning.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to citation insertions, adding 'Proceedings of' to the MOKA bibliography entry, and updating the arXiv version/date stamp. Substantive prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The citation additions produce small spacing and line-wrap changes in related work and references. All 16 figures and seven tables retain their content, captions, structure, and placement; appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly updates bibliographic coverage with two citations and a reference wording correction. It adds no substantive discussion, evidence, methodological clarification, or limitation analysis, and leaves all experimental and appendix content unchanged. These limited editorial updates do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
